claim: Layered bond structure (a small frequently contacted core and larger, rarer outer layers, each roughly 3x the last) emerges from a fixed contact budget plus per-bond decay and shared-experience amplification, without layer sizes being built in.

motivation.section: Q6 context 2026-11-11, Dunbar/valence chat (cited, not archived)
amplification amendment: best friend contact every 4 to 7 days

premortem: Any budget plus decay gives some spread of contact rates; the informative result is whether discrete layers with a stable size ratio appear, and how sensitive the ratio is to the decay and amplification parameters. The 4 to 7 day horizon number was tuned after a smoke run, so a weekly inner layer would not be independent confirmation.

experiment.world: Single agent allocating a weekly contact budget over N candidate bonds with closeness decay, amplification and reunion release; exact or near-exact optimizer.
experiment.arms: Budget sizes; decay half-lives; amplification on and off.
experiment.measure: Clustering of optimal contact frequencies into layers; layer size ratio.
experiment.test: Deterministic sweep; gap statistic or similar for layer count.

note: Prior work: Tamarit et al. derive layers from a fixed social resource (from the cited chat; verify).

claim: Chronic vacancy is a downward spiral: when a bond slot stays empty, threat vigilance rises and raises the cost of forming a new bond, so long-empty agents bond less than recently-emptied ones despite wanting more.

motivation.section: Q6 context 2026-11-11, Dunbar/valence chat (acute vs chronic vacancy; Cacioppo and Hawkley loneliness loop, verify)
upward and downward spirals

premortem: A vigilance term that raises bonding cost will produce the spiral by construction. The informative result is which rules or norms break it (lowering the cost of a first approach versus adding more contacts), mirroring the claim that fixing the lens beats adding reactants.

experiment.world: Household or network world with a vigilance state that rises with time alone and raises the cost of a first approach.
experiment.arms: No intervention; more contact opportunities; a norm that lowers first-approach cost.
experiment.measure: Time to first new bond; lifetime pleasure.
experiment.test: Permutation across personas; sweep over vigilance growth.

claim: Under free exit and shared-experience amplification, an agent maximizing only its own lifetime pleasure (egoist) chooses nearly the same policy as one maximizing the pair's total (utilitarian), because the partner's pleasure keeps the partner staying and amplifies shared activities. Remove free exit or amplification and the two policies diverge.

motivation.section: Q6 answer 2026-11-11 and the author's essay thesis that egoistic hedonists and hedonistic utilitarians alike must attend to others' pleasure
relationships as hedonic technology

premortem: If the partner's exit rule is tied to the partner's pleasure, some convergence is built in. The informative result is the size of the egoist-utilitarian gap and which mechanism (exit, amplification, giving pleasure) closes most of it, and a control where all three are off must show a large gap.

experiment.world: Two-agent horizon-style exact solve or the household world, with free exit, amplification and giving-pleasure as switchable mechanisms.
experiment.arms: Egoist vs utilitarian objective, crossed with each mechanism on or off (2 x 2 x 2 x 2).
experiment.measure: Policy distance and pleasure gap between egoist and utilitarian optima; the solitary (no-bond) persona's lifetime pleasure as a reference.
experiment.test: Exact where possible; sensitivity sweep over amplification and exit parameters.

note: Links the author's essay to the founding question: a mechanism (free exit plus amplification) that makes a self-interested agent care about another's welfare without training it to. Related to H01.

claim: First-time experiences are a non-renewable stock: each carries a one-time liking bonus and a high memory-vividness weight. A lifetime-pleasure optimizer spreads firsts over time and spends them in shared settings where amplification applies, while a greedy agent spends them early and alone, losing lifetime pleasure.

motivation.section: Q12 follow-up 2026-11-11: there is no replacing being surprised or experiencing something for the first time
vividness-weighted memory

premortem: A depleting stock with a positive amplification term will be spread and shared by an exact optimizer by construction. The informative result is the size of the greedy loss, and how it depends on the novelty spike vs liking split and on whether firsts are discovered (unknown in advance) rather than listed.

experiment.world: Horizon-style exact solve with a finite set of first-time experiences, each usable once, with a liking bonus, a vividness weight, and optional sharing amplification.
experiment.arms: Greedy vs lifetime optimizer; sharing on/off; firsts known in advance vs discovered.
experiment.measure: Lifetime pleasure; timing and sharing of firsts; greedy loss.
experiment.test: Exact; sweep over the first-time bonus and the vividness weight.

note: Builds on the novelty model (wanting spike, liking curve, learning progress) queued after test 1.

claim: Vivid cues amplify wanting at decision time without raising liking, so an environment that makes some options vivid (cues, imagery, reminders) widens the liking-wanting gap; a closure or reflection norm that brings the faint but higher-liking option to mind narrows it.

motivation.section: Support from the literature: Sinhababu
Decision 1 (test 1)

premortem: A vividness multiplier on wanting will widen the gap by construction. The informative result is whether a norm that raises the vividness of the alternative closes the gap more cheaply than removing the cue, and how it interacts with memory vividness weighting of liking.

experiment.world: The test 1 liking/wanting model (src/mar/wanting.py once committed) plus a vividness multiplier on wanting at choice time and memory vividness on liking.
experiment.arms: Plain; vivid cue on one option; vivid cue plus a reflection norm; cue removed.
experiment.measure: Liking per unit of wanting-driven activity; lifetime liking.
experiment.test: Exact or paired permutation as in test 1; sweep over the vividness multiplier.
